target_customer: Divorcing couples in the US, mostly those who want to settle without adversarial litigation
problem: Traditional divorce pushes each spouse to hire a lawyer, which is slow, costly and hard on children. Wevorce replaces this with a joint attorney-mediator process.
business_model: Tech-enabled legal services: fixed-fee divorce packages delivered by trained attorney-mediators
product_category: Online divorce mediation and legal services

founders.name: Michelle Crosby
founders.background_notes: YC page lists her as founder and CEO with no background. Search results describe her as a former family-law attorney but I did not open that source, so it is not recorded as fact.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly workflow software for intake, document generation and mediator scheduling, with the hard part being the legal and service process rather than engineering.

defensibility.rationale: The trained mediator network and process are an operational asset, but nothing sourced shows a structural barrier to a law firm or a document site copying the approach.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A Gizmodo item describes LegalZoom as working with Wevorce on its divorce platform, so the large online legal brand appeared as a partner rather than a copier.

market_need_then: The US average cost of a divorce was cited in 2013 coverage as about 27,000 dollars, against a Wevorce starting price of 749 dollars, so the stated pain was cost, conflict and effects on children.

identity.voice_and_tone: Humane and plain, with the founder describing the service as divorce for grown-ups per search coverage.

branding.community_and_virality: Coverage in ABC News, Entrepreneur, Business Insider and NPR affiliate WBEZ shows press interest in the concept.

brand_strength.rationale: The name makes the offering clear and drew national press, but no source shows community, merch or a brand asset beyond that.

outcome_analysis: Wevorce launched from YC in 2013, raised a 1.7 million dollar seed that November and a reported 3 million dollar Series A led by Techstars in 2016. The YC directory lists it as active, but a PitchBook page labels it out of business without a date, so the current state is unclear and no cause of failure is public.
notes: Company website returned 403 to fetch, so it was not read. Series A date of 2016-01 comes from CB Insights via a search summary and the amount from Business Insider; treat the date as approximate. Total raised conflicts across aggregators (4.75M, 6.4M, 7M, 8.31M). Search results name Jeff Reynolds as a co-founder, but no opened company source confirmed it, so he is not listed. PitchBook says out of business while YC says active; exit is recorded as none pending confirmation. No dated competitor sources near the batch were found.
